title: Compliance Evidence Forwarding Hub: verifiable delivery, backpressure, and configurable retention hints
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an intermediate 'Forwarding Hub' service that centralizes outbound compliance evidence delivery (audit events, residency/retention assertions, packaged evidence) with verifiable receipts, tenant-level delivery policies, and backpressure controls.

Background: Customers require deterministic evidence delivery for audits and residency proofs. Current shipper is per-service and has inconsistent retry/timeout semantics, limited observability, and no standardized proof-of-delivery. This ticket scopes a centralized component to standardize headers/metadata, provide signed delivery receipts, and expose webhook controls for retention/residency hints.

Success criteria:
- Canonical HTTP contract for evidence forwarding (see API summary below) implemented and documented.
- Idempotent delivery semantics with per-event ids and at-least-once with verifiable receipts for downstream consumers.
- Backpressure strategy: queue-depth watermarks, circuit-breaker thresholds, and per-tenant rate shaping.
- Support for per-event retention hints via header (X-RW-Retention-Hint) and residency assertions (X-RW-Residency-Region).
- Observability: per-tenant delivery latency SLI, failure breakdown, and end-to-end attestations available in Console.
- E2E tests + Github PRs and a staged rollout plan to 10 pilot customers.

API summary (high-level):
- POST /v2/evidence/forward -> accepts JSON event envelope, returns 202 + delivery_token. Envelope MUST include event_id, tenant_id, event_type, timestamp, and human-readable summary. Optional: retention_hint, residency_hint, references[].
- GET /v2/evidence/status/{delivery_token} -> returns delivery status (queued, delivering, delivered, failed) and last_attempt_ts.
- Callback semantics: target endpoints receive standard envelope plus X-RW-Delivery-Id, X-RW-Attestation (HMAC-SHA256 signature of body using per-tenant signing key), X-RW-Retention-Hint header.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts configurable per-tenant, and a dead-letter webhook endpoint support.

Implementation notes and decisions:
- We'll implement a small service using existing shipper infra (k8s service in staging) but with separate persistence (postgres) and a streaming queue (Redis streams initially) to manage ordering/visibility. This avoids touching the legacy per-service shippers until rollout.
- Signing: use tenant-managed KMS keys where available; fallback to platform key with tenant-scoped key id in header. Receipts are HMAC signatures over canonical JSON + delivery_token.
- Idempotency: event_id de-dup table with TTL aligned to retention_hint (min 7 days).
- Backpressure: token-bucket per-tenant plus total queue watermark. When high watermark reached, accept requests but mark as delayed and surface backpressure metric for Console and alerting.
- Retention hints: header values are strings like "ephemeral:7d", "standard:180d", "archival:3650d". These are advisory and drive downstream TTL choices and evidence packaging cadence.
- Residency: accept both single-region hint (e.g., "eu-west-1") and multi-region assertion. Evidence packages will include a residency_claim field set by the hub and signed in the attestation.

Observability and testing:
- Metrics: deliveries_total, deliveries_failed, avg_delivery_latency_ms, queue_depth_by_tenant, receipts_issued_total.
- Tracing: propagate parent trace id from incoming request; add links to delivery attempts.
- Tests: unit tests for signing/verification, integration tests mocking downstream webhooks with success/failure modes, and chaos test that simulates downstream slow/partial failures.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): implement contract and run integration tests with internal teams (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (pilot): enable hub for 10 low-risk tenants and mirror traffic from legacy shipper for comparison (4 weeks).
- Phase 3 (ramp): allow selected tenants to opt-in for primary delivery, continue mirror for others (4 weeks).
- Final cutover: migrate shipper config and deprecate legacy per-service shipper after 90 days of stable metrics.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Persistence choice (Redis streams vs Kafka). Redis streams faster to iterate but harder for long-term replay. Will revisit after pilot.
- Evidence packaging frequency vs retention costs. Need product input on default retention tiers.
- Whether hub should attempt on-platform redelivery to alternative endpoints on permanent downstream failure (fanout) or simply surface to DLQ and let customer handle.

- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-forwarder/pull/12 (WIP)
